# Skeema

Skeema is a tool for managing MySQL and MariaDB schema changes in a declarative fashion using pure SQL. The Skeema CLI tool allows you to:

* Export `CREATE TABLE` statements to the filesystem, for tracking in a Git repo
* Diff changes in the schema repo against live DBs to automatically generate DDL
* Manage multiple environments (e.g. dev, staging, prod) and keep them in sync with ease
* Configure use of online schema change tools, such as `pt-online-schema-change`, `gh-ost`, or `spirit`, for performing `ALTER TABLE`
* Apply configurable linter rules to proactively catch schema design problems and enforce company policies

Skeema supports a pull-request-based workflow for schema change submission, review, and execution. This permits your team to manage schema changes in exactly the same way as you manage code changes.

## Products and Downloads

This repo is the free open source Community edition of the Skeema command-line tool. The Community edition supports management of **tables** and **routines** (procs/funcs). Builds are provided for Linux and MacOS.

The paid Premium edition of the Skeema CLI adds support for managing **views**, **triggers**, and **events**. It also includes a native **Windows build**, built-in **SSH tunnel** functionality, **seed data** management, and many other improvements.

For download links and more information, visit [skeema.io](https://www.skeema.io/download/).

=== diff --help ===

Usage:  skeema diff [<options>] [<environment>]

Compares the schemas on database server(s) to the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema diff staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

The `skeema diff` command is equivalent to running `skeema push` with its
--dry-run option enabled.

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no differences were found; 1 if some
differences were found; or 2+ if an error occurred.

trial("sql in hidden dir",{".hidden/x.sql":"SELECT 1;\n","visible/y.sql":"SELECT 2;\n"})

import subprocess, os, tempfile, pathlib, re
def run(args,cwd):
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, env={**os.environ,"HOME":cwd})
    s=(p.stdout+"---ERR---\n"+p.stderr)
    s=re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d ','TS ',s)
    return p.returncode, s
def trial(label,files,cmds=[["diff"],["push"],["pull"]]):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        for k,v in files.items():
            p=pathlib.Path(td,k); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); p.write_text(v)
        print("===",label)
        for c in cmds:
            rc,o=run(c,td); print(c,rc,repr(o))

import pathlib,re,json

    txt=pathlib.Path(fname).read_text().splitlines()
    section=None
    print("CMD",cmd)
    for line in txt:
        if line.endswith(" Options:") or line=="Global Options:":
            section=line; continue
        # option lines start with 2 spaces - or 6 spaces --
        if re.match(r'^(  -|      --)',line):
            # split description at 2+ spaces after option spec? descriptions aligned col varies

            # Use regex capturing shorthand/long/value
            m=re.match(r'^(?:  -(.), )?      --|^(?:  -(.), )? {2,}',line)
            print(f" [{section}] {line}")
PY

import subprocess,os,re,tempfile,pathlib
def trial(fname,content,args=["init","--host=localhost","--port=-1"], envExtra=None):
 with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
  pathlib.Path(td,fname).write_text(content)
  e={**os.environ,"HOME":td}; 
  if envExtra: e.update(envExtra)
  p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=td,env=e)
  err=re.sub(r'\d{4}-..-.. ..:..:.. ','TS ',p.stderr).strip()
  return p.returncode,err
for sec in ["client","mysql","skeema","mysqld","server","foo","production","staging","client_mysql","mysql_client","client-skeema","skeemaclient","executable"]:
 rc,err=trial(".my.cnf",f"[{sec}]\nuser=alice{sec}\n")
 print(sec,rc, "alice"+sec in err, err[:230])
# what options read from my.cnf?
for opt,val in [("host","frommycnf"),("port","-2"),("socket","/tmp/x.sock"),("password","pw"),("user","bob"),("ssl-mode","disabled"),("ssl_mode","disabled"),("database","db"),("schema","db"),("default-character-set","utf8")]:
 rc,err=trial(".my.cnf",f"[client]\n{opt}={val}\n", args=["init","--host=localhost","--port=-1"] if opt!="host" else ["init","--port=-1"])
 print("opt",opt,rc,err[:400])
# skip-my-cnf still parses in v1? earlier deprecated warning says always in v2, v1 skip should skip
for extra in [[],["--skip-my-cnf"],["--my-cnf=false"]]:
 rc,err=trial(".my.cnf","[client]\nuser=alice\n",args=["init","--host=localhost","--port=-1"]+extra)
 print("skip",extra,rc,err[:300])

import subprocess,os,re,tempfile,pathlib
def run(files,actions,cmd="lint"):
 with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as home, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
  root=pathlib.Path(td)
  for k,v in files.items():
   p=root/k; p.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); p.write_text(v)

import re,pathlib,json
cmds=["add-environment","diff","format","init","lint","pull","push"]
info={}
for cmd in cmds:
 for line in pathlib.Path(f"/tmp/probe/{cmd}.txt").read_text().splitlines():
  if not re.match(r'^(  -|      --)',line): continue
  # option spec ends at alignment: descriptions start at a fixed align column that varies. Spec pattern
  m=re.match(r'^(?:  -(.+?),)?\s*--(?:\[skip-\])?([a-z0-9-]+)(\[=value\]| value)?(?:\s{2,}(.*))?$',line)
  if not m:
   print("NOMATCH",cmd,line); continue
  short=m.group(1); name=m.group(2); val=m.group(3) or ""; desc=m.group(4) or ""
  default=None; valid=[]
  dm=re.search(r'\(default "([^"]*)"\)',desc)
  if dm: default=dm.group(1)
  vm=re.search(r'\(valid values: ([^)]+)\)',desc)
  if vm: valid=re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"',vm.group(1))
  ent=info.setdefault(name,{"shorts":{},"commands":{},"hasvalue":val,"defaults":{},"valid":{}})
  ent["commands"][cmd]=desc
  if short: ent["shorts"][cmd]=short
  if default is not None: ent["defaults"][cmd]=default
  if valid: ent["valid"][cmd]=valid
  if val and ent["hasvalue"]!=val: print("val mismatch",name,ent["hasvalue"],val)
print(json.dumps(info,indent=1,sort_keys=True))
